q: A capacitor is used as an electric circuit component to store _____.

q: The capacitance of a capacitor is defined as the ratio of the _____ to the potential difference of the capacitor.
e: The capacitance of a capacitor is defined as the ratio of the charge to the potential difference of the capacitor. current and resistance belong to other processes, not this charge case. Charge is conserved; it is what a current carries and what a capacitor stores on its plates.

q: In the SI system, the unit of capacitance is _____.
e: In the SI system, the unit of capacitance is farad. coulomb is not farad, and volt is not farad either. One farad is one coulomb per volt, so practical capacitors are µF, nF or pF.

q: Therefore 1 F is equivalent to _____.
e: Therefore 1 F is equivalent to 1 C V^-1. Put 1 A s^-1 or 1 J C^-1 in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. One farad is one coulomb per volt, so practical capacitors are µF, nF or pF.

q: The equivalent capacitance C of the series combination of n identical capacitors, each of capacitance $C_1$, is C = _____.
e: The equivalent capacitance C of the series combination of n identical capacitors, each of capacitance C1, is C = C1/n. Put nC1 or n/C1 in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Two conductors and a dielectric hold opposite charge, so energy sits in the electric field. In series, the same current runs through each part and the voltages add.

q: In a parallel circuit diagram, the plates of the capacitors connected together at the point A have _____ charges.
e: In a parallel circuit diagram, the plates of the capacitors connected together at the point A have neutral charges. Put positive or negative in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. In parallel, the same voltage sits across each branch and the currents add. Parallel capacitors share voltage, charges add, and equivalent C is the sum.

q: In a series circuit diagram, the negatively charged plate of one capacitor is connected to the _____ charged plate of the other.
e: In a series circuit diagram, the negatively charged plate of one capacitor is connected to the positively charged plate of the other. negatively is not positively, and neutrally is not positively either. Two conductors and a dielectric hold opposite charge, so energy sits in the electric field.

q: There are two types of combination namely; (i) parallel and (ii) _____.
e: There are two types of combination namely; (i) parallel and (ii) series. Put circular or diagonal in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. In series, the same current runs through each part and the voltages add. In parallel, the same voltage sits across each branch and the currents add.
